description: Insufficient Data Encryption at Rest Data stored in AWS services is encrypted using service-managed keys rather than customer-managed KMS keys. While this provides basic encryption, it reduces control over key rotation and access. An attacker with access to AWS service-managed keys (through compromise or insider threat) could decrypt and access sensitive data across multiple storage services.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement AWS KMS customer-managed keys for all data storage services

description: Insecure QuickSight Dashboard Access Control QuickSight uses IAM roles and its own permission system for dashboard access. Misconfiguration can grant excessive permissions to users or groups. A user with basic QuickSight access could potentially view dashboards containing sensitive data from other business units due to overly permissive sharing settings.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1550 - Use Alternate Authentication Material
recommendation: Implement strict QuickSight access controls

description: Insufficient Audit Logging While basic CloudWatch logging is enabled, detailed audit trails of user actions, data access, and system changes are not comprehensively captured across all services. An attacker could perform unauthorized actions without detection, or clean up traces of their activities due to insufficient logging.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1562.008 - Impair Defenses: Disable Cloud Logs
owaspTop10: A09:2021-Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

description: Insecure API Gateway Configuration The API Gateway configuration lacks comprehensive authentication mechanisms and rate limiting, potentially allowing API abuse. An attacker could perform credential stuffing attacks or abuse API endpoints due to insufficient rate limiting and authentication controls.
references: recommendation: Enable request throttling and validation

description: Vulnerable Data Processing Pipeline Data ingested through Kinesis streams could contain malicious payloads that might exploit vulnerabilities in processing logic. An attacker could inject malformed data that crashes processing functions or manipulates analytics results.
references: recommendation: Enhance error handling and monitoring

description: EMR Cluster Security Vulnerabilities EMR clusters running in the VPC could be vulnerable to unauthorized access or privilege escalation if security groups and IAM roles are not properly configured. An attacker with access to the VPC could potentially access the EMR cluster and execute unauthorized analytics jobs.
